steps: القصة الحلوة يا بطل مش بتخلص في مكان واحد، دي ممكن تكون كذا صفحة وراء بعض! زي الكتاب اللي بنقرأه في المدرسة، صفحة البداية بتعرفنا الحكاية، وبعدين نقلب للصفحة اللي بعدها.
عشان نخلي الشخصية تتحرك من صفحة للثانية في سكراتش جونيور، بنستخدم بلوك الانتقال لصفحة جديدة. البلوك ده عامل زي باب سحري بياخدنا لصفحة تانية خالص بكل حاجة فيها.
البلوك ده بيشتغل لما الشخصية تدوس عليه أو تخلص كلام، فتقوم دايسة على البلوك وتقوم ناقلتنا فوراً للصفحة رقم 2 اللي فيها المغامرة الكبيرة بتاعة وسط القصة.
مثلاً، نعمل صفحة أولى فيها البطل نايم في بيته، ولما ندوس عليه يفتح باب الصفحة التانية اللي فيها الغابة العجيبة والشجرة اللي بتتكلم، والصفحة الثالثة فيها النهاية السعيدة.
القاعدة الذهبية هنا هي: رتب صفحاتك دايماً بالترتيب الصح من الشمال لليمين (بداية، وسط، نهاية) عشان القصة تكون واضحة وممتعة لأي حد هيتفرج عليها.
الفكرة دي بتستخدم في ألعاب الكمبيوتر الحقيقية ورسوم الكارتون، لما المستوي بيخلص واللاعب بيكسب، اللعبة بتنقله للمستوى اللي بعده في مكان تاني خالص.
ar.example: تخيل إنك بتصمم قصة عن قطة شجاعة. الصفحة الأولى فيها القطة في بيتها (البداية)، ولما بتدوس عليها بتنتقل للصفحة الثانية اللي فيها الكهف المظلم (الوسط)، وفي الآخر الصفحة الثالثة فيها الكنز (النهاية). بنحط بلوك الصفحة في آخر كل صفحة عشان ننقل القصة بسلاسة.
ar.mistake: الخطأ المشهور هو إننا نلخبط ترتيب الصفحات ونخلي النهاية قبل البداية! الحل هو إننا نتأكد من أسماء الصفحات وأرقامها في شريط الصفحات على اليمين قبل ما نشغل القصة.
ar.recap: تعلمنا إزاي نعمل قصة من كذا صفحة ونربطهم ببعض ببلوكات الانتقال. كده قصصنا بقت أكبر وأجمل!

q.why: شريط الصفحات بيكون ظاهر على يمين الشاشة عشان نشوف كل الصفحات.

steps: A wonderful story for a young hero doesn't just happen in one place; it can span multiple pages in a row! Just like a book we read at school, the opening page introduces the tale, and then we turn over to the next one.

To make our character move from one page to another in ScratchJr, we use the page-turn block. This block acts like a magical door taking us to a completely brand-new page with everything fresh inside it.
This block triggers when a character touches it or finishes talking, tapping the block and instantly transporting us to page number 2, where the big middle-story adventure awaits.

For example, let's create a first page where our hero sleeps at home, and when tapped, opens the door to page two featuring an enchanted forest and a talking tree, leading to page three for a happy ending.
The golden rule here is: always arrange your pages in the correct order from left to right (beginning, middle, ending) so the story remains clear and entertaining for anyone watching.
This exact concept is used in real computer games and cartoon shows; when a level finishes and the player wins, the game transitions them to the next level in a totally different setting.
en.example: Imagine designing a story about a brave cat. Page one shows the cat at home (beginning), and when tapped, it transitions to page two featuring a dark cave (middle), and finally page three shows the treasure (ending). We place the page block at the end of every page to transition smoothly.
en.mistake: A common mistake is mixing up the page order and putting the ending before the beginning! The fix is to check your page names and numbers on the right-side page strip before running your story.
en.recap: We learned how to create a multi-page story and link them together using transition blocks. Now our stories are bigger and much more wonderful!

q.t: Which block allows us to switch to another page in ScratchJr?
q.why: The page switch block is responsible for moving the character and story to a new page.

q.t: When starting a multi-page story, what should ideally be on the first page?
q.why: Stories always start with the beginning so viewers understand the tale from scratch.

q.t: Where can you find the page numbers and navigation strip in ScratchJr?
o: On the right side of the screen
q.why: The page strip appears on the right side of the screen to view all pages.

options: The story pauses and ends immediately
The story instantly jumps to page two and starts the middle events

sections.text: Long stories need multiple pages so they don't get crowded. Just like your schoolbook with a page for reading and a page for math, your ScratchJr story can be divided into separate pages for each part.
sections.code: Open book concept: Page 1, Page 2, Page 3
sections.output: Every page has its own space and unique characters

sections.text: This is the very first page of your story. We place the starting scenery here along with the main character greeting the audience or waking up. This sets up the 'Once upon a time' feeling.
sections.output: The first scene is ready to tell the tale's opening

sections.text: Here is where the challenge, problem, or adventure happens! This page features a different background like a forest or outer space, and the character performs exciting actions like running or flying.
sections.output: The second action-packed scene starts right away

sections.text: This is the final page of your wonderful story. This scene resolves the problem, and the character says 'The End' or dances happily after completing the grand adventure successfully.
sections.output: The story finishes in a happy and delightful way

sections.text: This is a magical red block featuring an arrow and a page icon. When placed at the end of our script, the character triggers it and shifts the entire scene to our chosen destination page.
sections.code: End of line: [Go to Page 2 block]
sections.output: Instant jump to the new page without closing the app

sections.text: To keep the story making sense, we must link page one to two, and two to three. If we scramble the order, the audience will get confused about where the story starts or ends.
sections.code: Page 1 -> links to -> Page 2 -> links to -> Page 3
sections.output: A well-ordered and logical chain of events

sections.text: To make our story look gorgeous and realistic, we change the background for each page. Page one might be daytime, page two nighttime, and page three outer space, for instance.
sections.code: Change background in property tray for each page
sections.output: Every page looks unique and captivating

sections.text: Before we finish our work, we must tap the green flag on page one and watch the story move through beginning, middle, and ending automatically without our interference.
sections.code: Run from Page 1 and watch automated page switching
sections.output: A fully cohesive and hundred-percent successful story
